title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Iran-linked water-utility PLC campaign holds at 12 states — and internet-exposed controllers are still the way in
items.content_text: Since 26–27 July, actors have reached internet-exposed Rockwell Automation Allen-Bradley MicroLogix 1100 and 1400 controllers at water and wastewater utilities in at least 12 states, changing device IP addresses and setting unauthorised passwords that lock operators out of monitoring and control. More than 30 Minnesota community systems were affected; Clayton County, Georgia issued a boil-water advisory after a pressure loss; later confirmed incidents hit Cape May and Woodbine, New Jersey and Childersburg, Alabama. Joint advisory AA26-097A — FBI, CISA, NSA, EPA, DOE, CNMF and Treasury — attributes the activity to Iranian-affiliated CyberAv3ngers actors tied to the IRGC, and agencies assessed the campaign still active as of 12 August. No CVE was exploited: the actors used the vendors’ own programming software against exposed controllers with weak or absent credentials. Several utilities ran manually for days. Officials maintain drinking-water safety was not compromised.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: FBI / CISA / NSA / EPA / DOE joint advisory AA26-097A — via IC3, SecurityWeek, Industrial Cyber
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Advisory published 7 Apr 2026, updated 22 Jul 2026; campaign assessed active as of 12 Aug 2026, 12-state total reported through 14 Aug 2026

items.title: Clop’s PLM extortion campaign now names Shell, GE and Philips — the stolen material is plant drawings and blueprints
items.content_text: Clop has listed 43 new victims tied to its exploitation of internet-exposed PTC Windchill and FlexPLM, the product lifecycle management platforms used across aerospace, defence, automotive, heavy machinery, medtech and retail. On 13 August Shell confirmed it is investigating a “potential incident” after the gang claimed 89 GB of data; on 17 August GE said it is assessing the claim and Philips confirmed a contained compromise of one enterprise server with no customer impact. The gang advertises backups, project plans, facility photographs, drawings, diagrams and blueprints. The entry point is CVE-2026-12569, an unsafe-deserialisation flaw in Windchill and FlexPLM rated CVSS 9.3 by ReliaQuest, exploited for unauthenticated remote code execution and JSP web-shell deployment. PTC began patching on 17 June and warned of heightened threat activity on 26 June; CISA added the flaw to KEV on 25 June with a three-day federal remediation deadline, and Germany’s BSI phoned customers overnight to push patching. No OT or control-system impact has been reported at any victim — this is confidentiality loss, not disruption. The OT relevance is what was taken: PLM holds the as-designed record of plants, machines and safety systems, and it is rarely inventoried as an OT-adjacent asset or covered by an OT threat model.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: BleepingComputer, Reuters, ReliaQuest, Ransom-ISAC, PTC advisory, CISA KEV
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Campaign reported 24 Jul 2026; Shell 13 Aug 2026; GE and Philips 17 Aug 2026

items.title: A confirmed nation-state actor pivoted through a shared private APN to stop a Polish CHP plant’s steam turbine
items.content_text: CERT Polska’s follow-up report on a 29 December 2025 intrusion describes an OT lateral-movement path most defenders have not modelled. The attacker started from a FortiGate appliance at a wind farm, used there as both firewall and VPN concentrator, and scanned the carrier-managed private APN for VNC, HTTP, Modbus and Siemens S7 services. That scan surfaced a WAGO PFC200 controller at an unrelated combined heat and power plant with a WAN-facing management interface and default credentials. The attacker enabled SSH, tunnelled into the plant’s OT network, and stopped the steam turbine and the process water treatment system; several ICS devices were permanently bricked during cleanup. The plant serves roughly 50,000 residents; heat and electricity deliveries were not interrupted. Polish reporting links the wider campaign, which reportedly targeted some 30 other energy sites, to Russia-linked activity. Researchers describe it as the first publicly documented use of a private APN as an OT lateral-movement path.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: CERT Polska follow-up report — via SecurityWeek
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Intrusion 29 Dec 2025; report and reporting 10–11 Aug 2026

items.title: A suspected China-nexus actor is mass-exploiting a patched vCenter flaw — the layer most OT DMZs now run on
items.content_text: CVE-2026-59310 is a directory-traversal flaw in the VMware vCenter Syslog server, CVSS 9.8, that lets a remote attacker with network access to vCenter execute arbitrary code. Broadcom patched it on 29 July; exploitation began on 3 August, five days later. German incident-response firm Quirso counted 361 victim IP addresses across 47 countries, with roughly half in Germany, the US, Turkey, Iran and France, and 343 of them already connected to attacker infrastructure by 5 August. Quirso assesses with moderate confidence a Chinese-speaking operator working in UTC+08:00. After compromise the actors drop the open-source reverse_ssh framework to hold an outbound channel that inbound filtering does not see; reporting describes at least one case ending in Babuk-derived ransomware. Victim IPs include hosting and cloud ranges, so the organisation count is unknown and no OT operator has been named. The OT relevance is structural rather than confirmed: at most modern plants vCenter hosts the historian, the HMI servers, the engineering jump host and the OT DMZ itself, so losing it stops production without an attacker ever touching a controller — the same pattern behind Dragos’s Q2 ransomware numbers.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Broadcom advisory; Quirso research — via SecurityWeek, The Hacker News
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Patched 29 Jul 2026; exploitation from 3 Aug 2026; reported 13 Aug 2026

items.title: A cyberattack forced all three North Carolina Ports facilities into manual operation — OT compromise not confirmed, but not ruled out either
items.content_text: An intrusion on 5 August, publicly reported the next day, disrupted operations at all three North Carolina State Ports Authority facilities: Wilmington, Morehead City, and the Charlotte inland terminal. A spokesperson confirmed an outside actor breached the IT system and that processing moved to manual procedures; the operator declined to say whether ransomware was involved. The breach is described as contained, with normal operating schedules resuming 6–7 August and some processing still manual. No compromise of crane systems or terminal-operating technology has been confirmed — but neither has it been explicitly ruled out, and the operator has not detailed the boundary between the breached IT environment and any OT.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Port operator statement — via The Record

items.title: A breach at logistics giant Ceva halted shipments from eight European warehouses and rippled into retail and gaming customers
items.content_text: Ceva Logistics, one of the largest global contract-logistics providers, suffered an intrusion on 29 July that disrupted part of its European contract-logistics business and stopped outbound shipments from eight warehouses. Customers were notified 1 August; the scale became public the week of 10 August. Ceva says air, ocean, ground and rail transport were unaffected and no other systems were touched. Personal data — names, addresses, phone numbers, emails and order details — was compromised; the company says payment and credential data were not. Downstream customers named include Bol, De Bijenkorf, Ace & Tate, Pokémon Center (UK and Germany, with some orders cancelled), Valve/Steam, Ajax and ING. The Dutch data-protection authority is investigating; no group has claimed the attack.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Ceva Logistics and customer disclosures — via The Record

items.title: US and South Korean agencies warn Gunra ransomware is walking in through unpatched edge appliances, not novel exploits
items.content_text: CISA, the FBI and South Korean counterparts published a joint #StopRansomware advisory, AA26-222A, on the Gunra operation, a Conti-derived ransomware-as-a-service group running double extortion against government and critical-infrastructure victims. Initial access is typically through unpatched internet-facing VPN gateways and exposed RDP rather than novel exploitation; the advisory cites Fortinet flaws CVE-2024-55591 and CVE-2025-24472 as vectors that remain unremediated at some victims. Gunra pressures victims with a five-to-seven-day payment deadline. The pattern matches what Dragos separately reported across industrial victims in Q2: entry through edge devices and remote-management tooling, valid-account abuse, and EDR-killer techniques once inside — not direct control-system manipulation.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA, FBI and South Korean agencies — joint advisory AA26-222A

items.title: Forescout counted 4,407 internet-exposed Rockwell controllers worldwide — 22 of them in cities hit by the water campaign
items.content_text: Forescout’s Vedere Labs found 4,407 internet-exposed Rockwell Automation and Allen-Bradley controllers worldwide, 2,844 of them in the United States, with the exposed population dominated by discontinued legacy MicroLogix 1400 and 1100 units — the same product lines targeted in the water-utility campaign. Cross-referencing against municipalities affected by that campaign turned up 22 devices still reachable from the open internet. Researchers concluded the intruders reconfigured devices directly rather than exploiting a new flaw, consistent with AA26-097A’s account of exposure and credential abuse rather than a CVE.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Forescout Vedere Labs — via The Hacker News, CyberScoop

items.title: A heavy-truck brake controller’s safety recall quietly doubled as a security fix — and nobody told the fleets
items.content_text: Researchers at the National Motor Freight Traffic Association reported that a safety recall issued for the Bendix EC80 electronic brake controller also closed remote code execution and denial-of-service weaknesses, without the security content being called out to operators. Fleets that treated the recall as a routine mechanical action would have had no reason to prioritise it as a cyber remediation, and any vehicle that skipped the campaign is still carrying the flaws. The pattern is the one OT asset owners keep meeting in a different costume: a safety-certified component gets a fix through a safety channel, the security implications never reach the people who track vulnerabilities, and the two remediation programmes never reconcile. The same dynamic applies to firmware shipped inside process skids, packaged equipment and vendor-maintained safety systems — and it means a clean vulnerability-management report can be entirely accurate and still miss patched-but-unapplied safety-critical defects.

items.title: Claroty Team82 found 23 flaws in Copeland refrigeration controllers — and showed a compromised unit can spoil stock while the temperature display stays normal
items.content_text: Team82 disclosed 23 vulnerabilities in Copeland XWEB Pro supervisory controllers, 21 of them rated high severity, plus multiple remote-code-execution flaws in Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration controllers. The Copeland set includes an authentication-middleware logic error that lets an unauthenticated request reach protected administrative API routes, and a deterministic password-generation scheme covering both SSH and web credentials. In a proof of concept the researchers turned off cooling fans and compressors from a compromised controller while the operator-facing temperature readout continued to show normal values — a manipulation-of-view outcome in an environment where the consequence is spoiled food or pharmaceuticals rather than a tripped process. Both vendors have shipped fixes; Copeland’s is firmware 1.13.

items.title: August ICS Patch Tuesday: a maximum-severity unauthenticated code-execution flaw in Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 leads a ten-advisory batch
items.content_text: Siemens’ headline fix is CVE-2026-58115, CVSS 10.0 (SSA-834709): missing authentication in Node-RED on SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices running Industrial OS lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker create flows and execute code at maximum privilege, with no credentials or user interaction required. It is fixed in firmware V4.3.4.1; interim options are removing Node-RED or hardening it per the Node-RED user guide. The same cycle fixed Siemens Siveillance Video (CVE-2026-3014, CVSS 9.1, OS command injection for a user with edit permissions), Siemens License Server (CVE-2026-69109 and CVE-2026-69108, CVSS ~7.5, an insecure sudoers policy and a path-traversal file-read issue), Schneider Electric NetBotz 5 (CVE-2026-13336, CVE-2026-13337, OS command and SQL injection, no verified CVSS) and PowerChute Serial Shutdown (CVE-2026-13348, an authentication-attempt-limit failure), and Phoenix Contact PLCnext (advisory VDE-2025-056, input-validation flaws enabling denial of service or malicious SQL execution; no CVE or CVSS verified). No confirmed exploitation has been reported for any of these as of this edition.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Siemens ProductCERT, Schneider Electric, Phoenix Contact

items.title: Haiwell’s IoT Cloud HMI gateway has an unauthenticated root-level remote code execution flaw, CVSS 10.0
items.content_text: CVE-2026-19188, confirmed CVSS 10.0 under both v3.1 and v4.0, is an OS command injection (CWE-78) in the Net Check feature’s cmdPing Socket.io event, reachable via the /setting endpoint on Haiwell IoT Cloud HMI Gateway devices. It grants an unauthenticated attacker root-level remote code execution. Version 3.40.1.12 is confirmed vulnerable; the fix ships in 3.50.1.19 or later. The gateway is deployed in energy and water/wastewater environments. An ICSA advisory number circulating for this flaw could not be independently confirmed — NVD is the citable source here.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: NVD (ICSA advisory number not independently confirmed)

items.title: Two critical deserialization flaws in Johnson Controls C-CURE 9000 and victor could hand attackers physical access-control systems
items.content_text: Johnson Controls’ C-CURE 9000 and victor security-management platforms carry two critical unauthenticated deserialization flaws, CVE-2026-21655 and CVE-2026-21653, plus a high-severity issue, CVE-2026-34496, with CVSS scores up to 9.6. A network-adjacent attacker could exploit the deserialization bugs to execute code and take over the physical access-control system they run — doors, badges and access logs. CISA’s advisory (ICSA-26-204-01) was updated (Update A) on 11 August. No exploitation has been confirmed.

items.title: CISA published 15 ICS advisories in a single day, spanning AVEVA, Hitachi Energy, ANDRITZ and more
items.content_text: CISA released 15 industrial control system advisories on 13 August. AVEVA Enterprise SCADA and HMI carry CVE-2025-7639 (CVSS 7.1), untrusted deserialisation letting an authenticated operator-privilege user execute code; fixes exist across every supported release line. Hitachi Energy’s APM Edge transformer-monitoring appliance carries two Linux-kernel-inherited flaws, CVE-2026-43284 and CVE-2026-43500 (NVD CVSS 8.8 and 7.8) — sources conflict on whether firmware is available, so patch status should be confirmed directly with the vendor advisory. ANDRITZ HIPASE-250 and 250 SCALA protection devices ship with a fixed VNC password baked into the provisioning script and an unauthenticated, permissively configured API exposing live process data; no CVSS could be verified for these. Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808, used to host applications at substations, carries an XSS and a path-traversal flaw (CVSS 6.1/5.5) from bundled Fortinet components. Johnson Controls updated Airwall, an OT secure-remote-access product, for a hardcoded cryptographic key and a path-traversal file-read issue (CVSS 6.8/6.4), fixed in 4.1.0. None of the 15 is currently reported as exploited.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA ICS advisories — corroborated by WaterISAC TLP:CLEAR bulletin

items.title: Cisco ASA and FTD join CISA’s KEV catalogue for an actively exploited flaw that crashes firewalls on demand
items.content_text: CVE-2026-20349, CVSS 8.6, is a heap-inspection denial-of-service flaw in the Remote Access SSL VPN service of Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD software. It is actively exploited in the wild to crash devices and was added to CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 11 August with a 14 August federal remediation deadline, which has now passed. Hotfixes are available across all affected 9.x, 7.x and 10.x branches; there is no workaround. ASA and FTD are commonly deployed as the IT/OT boundary device carrying vendor and engineering remote access into plant networks.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV catalogue and Cisco advisory — via BleepingComputer

items.title: A CVSS 10.0 SAP Commerce Cloud flaw is being probed within days of the patch — and industrial operators run SAP everywhere
items.content_text: CVE-2026-58231 is an improper-authorisation flaw in the Data Hub Adapter for SAP Commerce Cloud, rated CVSS 10.0, that lets an unauthenticated attacker with network access abuse a default authentication client and submit crafted input to functions that do not validate it — ending in arbitrary code execution and compromise of internal components. SAP shipped the fix in its 11 August Security Patch Day alongside 27 other notes. Threat-intelligence firm Defused Cyber saw exploitation attempts hit its honeypots three days later, on 14 August, while noting the flaw has no public proof-of-concept and is not known to have been successfully exploited. SAP security firm Onapsis says an IP Filter Set restricting access to the vulnerable endpoint works as a temporary workaround. This is an enterprise-side flaw with no direct control-system reach, and it is here because SAP is the system of record sitting immediately upstream of production scheduling, spares, maintenance and shipping at most industrial operators — the same enterprise layer whose loss stopped plants in Dragos’s Q2 figures without an attacker ever reaching a controller.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: SAP Security Patch Day; Defused Cyber and Onapsis — via The Hacker News
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Patched 11 Aug 2026; exploitation attempts observed 14 Aug 2026; reported 15 Aug 2026

items.title: The Water Cyber Shield Act would give EPA mandatory-assessment authority and $300M a year for utility cybersecurity
items.content_text: Senators Klobuchar and Schiff introduced the Water Cyber Shield Act on 13 August, three weeks into the multistate PLC campaign. The bill would give EPA authority to require mandatory cybersecurity assessments of water and wastewater systems, direct $300 million a year through state revolving funds for security improvements, and require large water systems to build cyber risk into their resilience planning. It has not been enacted.

items.title: A volunteer-built “Water Watch Center” launched at DEF CON to put paid monitoring into the smallest utilities — the ones the campaign is hitting
items.content_text: DEF CON Franklin and the National Rural Water Association launched the Water Watch Center, aimed squarely at utilities serving fewer than 10,000 people — about 91% of the roughly 50,000 US community water systems, and the segment with no security staff at all. Five firms — Defendify, Legato Security, L1 Secure, Rapid7 and Sentinel Technologies — will deliver managed detection and response directly to participating utilities, with threat intelligence shared back through the NRWA. Seed funding came from Craig Newmark. The programme builds on a two-year pilot that paired roughly 450 volunteer practitioners with utilities in seven states, is expanding into Maryland, and is working with Vanderbilt on digital twins of water environments under DARPA’s CASTLE research.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: DEF CON Franklin and National Rural Water Association — via SecurityWeek
